source.title: Weak-to-Strong Search: Align Large Language Models via Searching over Small Language Models
source.authors: Zhan-Hui Zhou; Zhi-Xuan Liu; Jie Liu; Zhichen Dong; Chao Yang; Yu Qiao

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper builds and evaluates a test-time search method using smaller tuned and untuned models as guidance. It does not test fine-tuning a strong student on labels produced by a weak supervisor, or measure PGR.
record.gate_note: The paper calls its test-time search an instance of weak-to-strong generalization, but its intervention is decoding-time guidance from small-model log-probability differences, not training on weak-produced labels. The paper's CBS results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version; no claim version is tested. The paper's hyperparameter ablations and comparisons among CBS, EFT and BoN are not recorded as claim results.
record.test_reason: The paper introduces Chunk-level Beam Search, a test-time method that steers a frozen large model with the log-probability difference of small tuned and untuned models. It calls this an instance of weak-to-strong generalization, but no strong model is trained on weak labels and no PGR or strong ceiling is measured. In the instruction-following runs the large models already beat the weak guide before search, so the setup is not V1's question. The one training result is a preliminary PPO run in Appendix C.3 using a weak-model reward. It is figure-only and uses a reward signal, not labels, so it does not make this a test of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that weak-to-strong search aligns frozen large models via test-time search over small tuned/untuned models, effective in sentiment generation, summarization and instruction following (white-box and black-box). They frame this as weak-to-strong generalization that makes strong models stronger with weak test-time guidance. They also report preliminary evidence that the dense weak-model reward helps PPO fine-tuning, with weak-to-strong generalization during training (Appendix C.3).
record.recipe_differences: Uses test-time chunk-level search guided by the log-probability difference of small tuned and untuned models; the large model remains frozen and is not trained on weak-produced labels.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that CBS outcomes vary with beam width, successors per state and chunk length, and that the best W/K trade-off differs between controlled-sentiment generation and summarization. Instruction-following settings also use different CBS parameters across models and black-box versus white-box models.

fits_no_version.finding: Test-time search guided by small tuned/untuned model pairs raises frozen large models' AlpacaEval 2.0 LC win rates. Examples: Llama-3-70B-Instruct 34.42→37.92 under Zephyr guidance; gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct 16.00→20.07. This holds even though the guiding zephyr-7b-beta scores only 13.20 and tulu-2-dpo-7b 9.46. The paper also reports gold-reward gains on sentiment and summarization (figure only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Decoding-time search guided by a weaker tuned/untuned model pair can improve a stronger frozen model beyond both its own baseline and the weak guide.

record.problems: The reported intervention is test-time search rather than weak-label fine-tuning, so its results cannot establish PGR or the claim versions. Instruction-following win rates use gpt-4-turbo as judge; uncertainty is not stated for the tabulated win rates. The paper reports mean ± standard deviations across three seeds for the reward figures.
record.rows_left_out: CBS hyperparameter ablations and comparisons among CBS, BoN, EFT and other methods were omitted because they evaluate the paper's introduced method rather than the weak-label fine-tuning intervention. Additional results appear in Figures 4–9 and Tables 2–4.

untested.parts: Fine-tuning a strong model on weak-model labels, the strong ceiling, and PGR. Only a figure-only PPO run with a weak-model reward exists (Appendix C.3).
Training changes to weak-label fine-tuning and their effect on PGR.
How PGR varies with supervisor or student size, task, or representations.
All failure modes. The authors raise them only as future work.
Theory of when a student must beat its supervisor.

missing.what: PPO fine-tuning of gpt2-large and Llama-2-7b (LoRA) using a dense reward from tuned/untuned gpt2. The authors say weak-to-strong generalization occurs because students exceed the weak π*'s gold reward of about 4.6. No numbers are given and no strong ceiling is reported, so PGR can't be computed.
missing.versions: V1 (loosely; reward-based weak supervision, not labels)

missing.what: The weak guide models' own scores, which are the reference point for the paper's weak-to-strong framing. LC WR: zephyr-7b-beta 13.20, mistral-7b-sft-beta 7.54, tulu-2-dpo-7b 9.46, tulu-2-7b 9.03.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T4 and no-version judgment is kept. The paper uses 'weak-to-strong' for test-time guidance, where the strong model already outperforms the weak guide; this is not the PGR setup. Appendix C.3 is the closest result to V1, but it is figure-only, preliminary, reward-based and has no strong ceiling, so no verdict is given. Rows r1–r8 are figure-only, so their 'observed' state cannot be checked numerically.

versions.untested_parts: Fine-tuning a strong model on weak-model-produced labels; beating the weak supervisor; PGR.
Training changes to weak-label fine-tuning and their effects on PGR.
PGR variation by supervisor/student size, task or representation; the paper varies models and tasks for test-time search, not weak-label fine-tuning.
The specified weak-label fine-tuning failure modes.
Conditions under which a student trained on weak labels must outperform its supervisor.

relation.reason: The method uses weak-to-strong guidance to steer frozen models and reports its own performance; the listed experiments do not test any specified claim version.

tranche.reason: The listed results evaluate the authors' test-time search method using weak guidance, without testing the catalog's weak-label fine-tuning or PGR claims.

source_check.notes: All listed rows are the study's own method comparisons and should not serve as claim-result rows. Appendix C.3/Figure 9 additionally trains gpt2-large and Llama-2-7b with PPO using weak-model dense rewards, so a blanket claim that the entire study keeps strong models frozen is inaccurate.
